Note::take¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::take(pluss::RangeView<std::int64_t> indices) const
Note Note::take(const Note& indices) const

The range overload accepts a braced list {0, 2, 4}, a std::vector<std::int64_t>, a std::array, or a std::span. The closed overload accepts an Int64 Note, including the direct result of argsort().

Gather Cells By An Index List¶

take(indices) treats the Note as its flat row-major sequence of cells and returns a rank-1 Note containing the cells at the given positions, in the order listed. Unlike select and narrow, which take a contiguous slab along one axis, take picks arbitrary positions — so it can also reorder, repeat, filter, or subsample cells in a single call.

The receiver may use any Note dtype. Text and Bytes results share the packed source arena and allocate only new span metadata; Bool, Int64, and Float64 results allocate one aligned lane buffer and copy the selected native values. The dtype always carries over, and the cost is O(len(indices)).

indices¶

  • Each index addresses a cell in the flattened Note: for a 2 × 3 grid the valid range is 0 .. 5, row-major ((0,0) (0,1) (0,2) (1,0) …). Input of any rank is accepted; the result is always rank 1.

  • A negative index counts from the end: -1 is the last cell. After that adjustment it must be in [0, numel()), otherwise Note::take index out of range.

  • Indices may repeat and appear in any order — the result mirrors the list exactly.

  • An empty indices returns a rank-1 Note of length 0.

  • An index Note must be defined and Int64. Its own rank is immaterial because its lanes are consumed in flat row-major order.

Example 1: Gather A Subset¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.take({0, 2, 4})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["a", "c", "e"]

Example 2: Negative Indices And Repeats¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.take({-1, -1, 0})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["f", "f", "a"]

-1 resolves to "f" and may be used more than once.

Example 3: Reversing With A Full Index List¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.take({5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["f", "e", "d", "c", "b", "a"]

Example 4: Higher-Rank Input Is Flattened First¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.take({0, 3, 5})) << "\n";     // (0,0) (1,0) (1,2)

const auto t = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"}).reshape({1, 2, 3});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(t.take({1, 4})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["a", "d", "f"]
Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["b", "e"]

The 2 × 3 and 1 × 2 × 3 inputs are read row-major; the result is a plain list regardless.

Example 5: Scalar Input And An Empty List¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note("solo").take({0, 0})) << "\n";

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.take(std::vector<std::int64_t>{})) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["solo", "solo"]
Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

A 0-D scalar has one cell at index 0; an empty list yields an empty rank-1 Note.

Example 6: Out-Of-Range Index¶

try {
  (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b"}).take({5});
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

Note::take index out of range

Example 7: Keep Sorting Inside The Note Family¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make({"delta", "alpha", "charlie", "bravo"});
const pluss::Note order = values.argsort();
const pluss::Note sorted = values.take(order);

std::cout << pluss::note::print(order) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::note::print(sorted) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, dtype=Int64)
[1, 3, 2, 0]
Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta"]

No .integers() extraction is required: the ordering remains an Int64 Note until take() consumes it.

Passing a Bool, Text, Bytes, or Float64 Note as indices throws before the receiver is read.

See Also¶

  • Note::select: one slab along one axis, that axis dropped.

  • Note::narrow: a contiguous range along one axis, rank kept.

  • Note::flatten: the row-major reading order take indexes into.
